To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the attitude toward system use plays an important role in explaining the intention of captive users to use the system and that the intention to use is not a good predictor of use.
the model we developed explains the use of mandatory systems well and that attitude plays a more important role than intention in explaining system use in mandatory settings.
mandatory use of information systems is not a good predictor of use and that attitude toward use, a second-order construct, is a good predictor of mandatory system use, while intention to use is not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: “How do we design and manage systems to ensure their effective use by mandatory users?”
the design and evaluation of systems in mandatory settings.
the use of information technology in mandatory settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mandatory systems can be designed to increase the likelihood of use, and the likelihood of use can be increased through design.
mandatory use is a very complex phenomenon that cannot be explained in terms of a single model.
our study provides a new model of use for mandatory systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TAM, the de facto standard for understanding technology acceptance, does not apply in mandatory settings.
a mandatory system can be used effectively if its design and use are informed by the three levels of abstraction.
the informing science approach provides a framework for studying system use and for developing a model for mandatory use of information systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TAM, a widely used model for voluntary system use, cannot be applied to mandatory systems without modifications.
mandatory use of software technologies is possible and that the informing science perspective can be used to design systems that are more likely to be used.
the informing science perspective can be used to integrate findings from disparate literatures into a model for mandatory use of information systems.
